absent: Locking discipline, interrupt context, preemption and concurrency requirements for reset and VMCS setup paths.
Full layouts of per virtual CPU, per VM, nested control, posted descriptor and tracing structures beyond fields touched here.
Semantics of identifier synchronization, APIC reload handling, user return MSR setup and constant host state caching beyond invocation.
Exact numeric encodings of pin, primary, secondary, tertiary, entry and exit control bits and VMCS field identifiers.
Callers, ordering guarantees and error handling for reset entry points and SGX policy helpers.

findings.text: Lifecycle helpers in this lane are callable across compilation units for virtual CPU reset, constant host state, guest host mask control, nested shadowing bitmap setup, SGX launch key shadowing and ENCLS bitmap policy. Reset distinguishes initialization events from full resets, while SGX and nested helpers provide firmware enablement and nested exit queries used during baseline configuration.

Virtual CPU reset clears software tracking for real mode activity, speculation control, wait control and hypervisor deadline, resets virtual interrupt priority, rebuilds guest segments and descriptor tables to power on real mode like values, clears segment caches and marks them available, places the guest in active state with no blocking or pending debug or injected event, conditionally clears bound configuration and control flow state when host capabilities exist, then requests APIC page reload, synchronizes identifier context and refreshes the buffer clearing disable flag. Full reset additionally rebuilds the whole VMCS baseline, while initialization events skip that rebuild.

Segment initialization establishes flat zero base descriptors with full sixty four kibibyte limit and present writable data attributes, with the code descriptor additionally marked as code. Reset then overrides code selector and base to the conventional reset vector region, clears task and local descriptor selectors and bases while retaining full limits and present system types, and clears global and interrupt table bases with full limits.

Posted interrupt notification state is constrained to one of two architected vectors, initialized to the normal posted vector with suppress notification set, with VMCS vector and descriptor address programmed from the same vector and descriptor location when kernel based APIC virtualization is active. Nested posted notification starts disabled and nested pointers start invalid.

Fill buffer clearing disable is permitted only when automatic host clearing is off, host capability advertises disable control, and host is unaffected by the relevant transient execution issues. The disable is suppressed when guest capability shows VERW clearing is already handled or when guest reports immunity across the sampling related capability family, in which case no entry interception work is needed.

ENCLS exit control defaults to intercepting every leaf when hardware support exists and guest SGX is not enabled. When guest exposes SGX and firmware enables it, creation and tracking leaves are released unless creation must be intercepted, augmentation and modification leaves are released when second generation SGX is exposed, initialization is always intercepted when host launch control exists, and any nested hypervisor requested interceptions are merged, consulting current nested controls when running nested without an explicit nested structure.

Guest firmware SGX enablement requires both enable and lock bits in the guest feature control shadow. Creation leaf interception is required when provisioning is disallowed or when guest SGX capability leaves are missing or diverge from host values, otherwise creation is allowed to proceed without interception.

Full reset shadows the host launch enclave public key hash into per virtual CPU storage, with a no operation fallback when SGX is compiled out. Launch control registers are intentionally not switched on entry or exit, and initialization handling uses guest values even when fixed to defaults.

Baseline execution controls start from global VMCS configuration and are masked by runtime policy. Pin controls follow APIC virtualization activity and global enables for posted interrupts, virtual NMIs and preemption timing. Primary controls reserve timestamp, I O bitmap, monitor trap and pause handling for nesting, leave window controls for dynamic toggling, and adapt debug, shadowing, priority, paging, wait and halt interceptions to debug state, shadowing need, paging mode and guest permissions. Secondary and tertiary controls adapt APIC, identifier, paging, unrestricted execution, pause loop, register virtualization, delivery, extended mode, function, execution mode, descriptor, shadow, logging, extended state, timestamp counter, invalidation, random, wait package, bus lock, notify and IPI features to hardware support, global enables, guest exposure and virtualization activity.

Exit and entry MSR areas start empty with addresses pointing at per virtual CPU automatic buffers, page fault masks and target count start cleared, link pointer starts invalid, function control starts cleared, and guest PAT is initialized only when entry loading of PAT is configured. Exit and entry control words start from global configuration with tracing, CET, mode and performance bits adjusted for host mode and support, and several save and load bits are forced off for dynamic handling or nesting emulation.

Constant host state captures current host control registers, kernel code and data selectors with cleared data selectors on sixty four bit, task selector, host table base and exit resume point, plus system entry, PAT, extended feature, CET and performance fields conditioned on configuration and hardware support. Filesystem and global segment bases are cleared to required values, with system entry stack handling differing by thirty two bit emulation availability.

Guest owned control register bits are derived from the hypervisor allowed set minus reserved bits, with flush and pointer bits removed when extended paging is disabled and with nested masked bits removed when running nested. The complement is programmed as the guest host mask for both control registers, with the zero register mask derived from first level guest owned bits.

Observed reset and baseline writes touch a defined subset of per virtual CPU and per VM state including real mode flag, speculation and wait controls, hypervisor deadline, nested feature shadows and pointers, SGX key hash and feature control validity, microcode version under a quirk, posted descriptor, logging window and dirty flag, tracing descriptor, performance and notification configuration and user return state. Descriptor table, segment, activity, interception, bitmap, APIC virtualization, logging, tracing and debug VMCS fields are established during baseline and reset phases.

Reset sequencing proceeds through optional full baseline rebuild, software tracking clear, architectural segment and table rebuild, cache clear and availability mark, activity and interception clear with capability conditional zeroing, APIC reload request, identifier synchronization and mitigation refresh. Baseline establishment precedes architectural rebuild and covers link, controls, bitmaps, APIC structures, paging, logging, tracing, system entry, debug and host state before guest state is finalized.

Correctness hazards include a diagnostic if host task switched flag is set, non atomic sampling of host paging base, inability to enable shadow VMCS during baseline for lack of nested controls, shared control for timestamp counter instructions allowing both when either is exposed, forced clearing of function and descriptor controls despite base configuration, and deliberate omission of launch control register switching due to cost.

Guest power on values use code selector F000 with base FFFF0000, data selectors zero with base zero, limit FFFF for segments and tables, data attributes 93 with code bit for code, task attributes 8B and local descriptor attributes 82, active activity with zero blocking, pending debug and entry injection, hypervisor deadline minus one, and tracing output mask 7F with low bits forced.

Full reset uses invalid guest physical and invalid mediated control sentinels for nested pointers with posted notification minus one, microcode version one shifted by thirty two under the feature MSR quirk, feature control valid bits locked only, link invalid, MSR counts zero, fault masks and target count zero, system entry and debug zero, and ENCLS bitmap all ones when SGX is unavailable or disabled.

Host baseline uses kernel code selector for code and kernel data selector for stack with cleared data selectors on sixty four bit, task selector from task state table entry, cleared filesystem and global bases, resume to the VM exit handler, and zeroed performance global control on exit when mediated monitoring is enabled.
